 Search “The Final Table” Episodes 1–2 Review: Is This K-Drama Worth Your Watchlist?
 Disha Paul 21 hours ago 5 min read A talented chef, a restaurant on the verge of closing, and a powerful company with something to hide. The Final Table has all the ingredients for a gripping K-drama, but its opening two episodes have to do more than serve up pretty dishes to keep viewers interested. 
 The Final Table Episodes 1–2 Review: A New K-Drama Worth Watching? (JTBC) Starring Ahn Hyo-seop as Kang Han and Hong Hwa-yeon as Choi Song-yi, the JTBC drama centers on  The Table: K-Chef 2026 , a high-stakes competition that brings together talented Korean chefs to compete for recognition. 
 However, the real conflict begins before the first official challenge, when two people connected to the same restaurant find themselves on opposite sides of a painful misunderstanding. 
 Episodes 1 and 2 introduce the characters, the family histories behind their ambitions, and the corporate controversy that could shape the competition. The result is a promising start, although the drama still has some work to do before it becomes a must-watch. 
 The Final Table (JTBC) The Final Table Episodes 1 and 2 Recap 
 Spoilers ahead for both episodes. 
 Episode 1: Kang Han's Visit Turns Into a Disaster 
 Kang Han ( Ahn Hyo-seop ) is a gifted chef who has spent much of his professional life working overseas. Before leaving South Korea again, he visits Famiglia, a restaurant connected to a cherished memory of his late father. He expects to find the food that once made the place special to him. 
 Instead, the meal disappoints him. Unable to understand why the restaurant has fallen so far below the standard he remembers, Han storms into the kitchen and openly criticises the food. 
 Unfortunately, he has no idea what has happened to the restaurant. 
 Choi Song-yi ( Hong Hwa-yeon ), Famiglia's manager and daughter of its former owner-chef, Choi Seung-hyo ( Jang Hyun-sung ), is already struggling to keep the business alive. Her father's reputation has been damaged following a conflict with Pyeongyeon Group, a powerful company in the food industry. 
 Customers have stopped coming, employees are leaving, and even securing supplies has become difficult. 
 The Final Table (JTBC) Song-yi is also dealing with her father's death while trying to defend his name. Han's criticism therefore lands at a particularly painful moment. To him, the food represents a treasured memory that has been ruined. To her, his words are another reminder of the restaurant and family she is desperately trying to protect. 
 Their first meeting quickly becomes confrontational, and neither has the full picture of the other's circumstances. 
 Meanwhile, Pyeongyeon Group is preparing a major culinary competition called The Table: K-Chef 2026 . Seon Jeong-won ( Jung Yoo-jin ), a producer involved in organising the event, sees the competition as an opportunity to bring Korean cuisine to a wider audience. 
 However, the company's interest in the event is complicated by the controversy surrounding Famiglia. 
 The episode ends with a sudden kitchen accident that interrupts Han and Song-yi's confrontation. Their disastrous introduction leaves one question hanging: can these two people find common ground when they barely understand each other? 
 Episode 2: Song-yi Chases Han to the Airport 
 The second episode gives Song-yi a practical reason to put her pride aside. She needs a way to save Famiglia, and entering The Table: K-Chef 2026  could bring the restaurant back into the public eye. 
 There is just one problem. She needs a chef capable of competing, and Kang Han is preparing to leave for the United States. 
 Song-yi tracks him down at the airport and asks him to stay. Her request is not simply about keeping the restaurant open. She wants to restore her father's reputation and challenge the company she believes is responsible for his downfall. 
 Han initially has little reason to become involved. He has his own plans, and their first meeting gave him every reason to walk away. But Song-yi's determination and the details of her father's situation begin to change the way he sees the conflict. 
 The Final Table (JTBC) The episode also reveals a more personal connection between Han and the controversy. He has his own painful history involving Pyeongyeon Group and the loss of his father. Song-yi's words force him to reconsider whether leaving Korea is really the right decision. 
 The culinary competition itself is not a last-minute project created after Famiglia's crisis. Jeong-won has been developing it for years, hoping to establish Korean cuisine on the global stage. The company's interest in using the event to manage the controversy gives the competition another layer of tension. 
 By the end of Episode 2, Han agrees to participate in the competition alongside Song-yi. What began as a disagreement over a disappointing meal now has the potential to become a partnership built around shared loss and a common adversary. 
 The story finally has a direction beyond their first clash. The real test will be whether they can work together once the competition begins. 
 The Final Table Episodes 1 and 2 Ratings: Is It Performing Well? 
 The drama premiered on JTBC on October 24, 2026 . According to reports citing Nielsen Korea, Episode 1 recorded approximately 1.9% nationwide viewership, while Episode 2 rose to around 2.4%. 
 That increase is encouraging for the early run, but two episodes are not enough to establish whether the drama will become a ratings success. Its longer-term performance will depend on whether the cooking competition, family stories, and character relationships can keep viewers engaged. 
 For now, the opening has established a central conflict and given Han a reason to stay. The next episodes will need to turn that setup into a more gripping competition. 
 The Final Table Episode 1 and 2 Review: Watch It or Skip It? 
 Watch it.   The Final Table is worth sampling if you enjoy K-dramas that combine food, professional ambition, family conflict, and a developing relationship. 
 The opening two episodes are not flawless. The story introduces a lot of background information, and Kang Han's sharp attitude may frustrate viewers who prefer instantly likeable leads. However, Famiglia's emotional importance and Song-yi's determination give the drama a foundation that goes beyond cooking spectacle. 
 Episode 2 is the stronger turning point because it gives Han and Song-yi a shared goal. Their agreement to enter the competition sets up a conflict in which success could mean much more than winning a title. 
 We would recommend continuing for the next couple of episodes, especially if you enjoy watching talented characters compete while dealing with personal stakes. If you are looking for a fast-paced romance from the very first episode, you may want to wait and see how the relationship develops. 
 Final Thought 
 The Final Table has a promising premise, a compelling reason for its leads to work together, and enough unresolved conflict to keep the story moving. It has not reached its full potential yet, but it has given viewers a good reason to return for the next course. 
 Would you keep watching The Final Table after Episodes 1 and 2, or did the slow setup make you want to skip it?
